Seminar Title:

Development of Clean-Label, Sustainable, and Functional Bakery Systems for Food Processing Applications

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Debmalya Banerjee ( Rollno : 523bm1006)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

20 Nov 2026 5:00 PM

Contact:

Kunal Pal

Abstract:

Bread is one of the most globally consumed staple foods, with whole wheat bread (WWB) offering substantial nutritional benefits over its refined counterpart. Nevertheless, the coarse bran particles present in whole wheat flour (WWF) introduce several technological limitations, including densification of the crumb and a reduced loaf volume. In this context, hydrocolloids have emerged as structural modulators that are used to improve the overall performance of the WWB systems. Although several investigations have been performed on the effect of traditional hydrocolloids on bakeries, the impact of gellan gum (GeG), a microbial, clean-label polysaccharide, remains underexplored. At the registration seminar (August 2025), the research framework was designed around four objectives encompassing GeG in baked and steamed WWB and banana peel powder (BPP). Since then, the first part of Objective 1 has been published in Food Hydrocolloids (2026), wherein 0.125% w/w GeG exhibited the most balanced alignment with the control, including comparable textural attributes, preserved viscoelasticity, and molecular homogeneity. Building upon these findings, a second investigation was performed on nine formulations (0&ndash2% w/w GeG) using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) analysis, electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) with (RQ)Q equivalent-circuit modeling, and dehydration kinetics. Interestingly, GeG induced non-monotonic changes in the microstructural, electrical, and dehydration characteristics, and GG0.125 exhibited organized pores, comparatively low equivalent-circuit resistance (RRQ = 2115.137 &plusmn 18.500 &Omega), and substantial cumulative dehydration (52.15% at 720 min). In light of these observations, the objectives have been revised to progress from GeG in bread toward GeG/guar gum binary gels, rice bran oil emulgels, and candelilla wax bigels, followed by their application in the optimized WWB system. This report presents the revised objectives, the work plan, and the progress achieved so far.
